summary: This Dockerfile creates a PHP 8.2 development image with code quality tools (PHP-CS-Fixer and PHPCBF), Composer for dependency management, and a non-root user for running the application. It sets up directories, installs necessary Linux packages, and configures environment variables like timezone and Composer cache location.

explanations.1: This sets a default PHP version that can be overridden when building the image, making the Dockerfile reusable across different PHP versions.
explanations.3: This defines where Composer (PHP's package manager) stores its cache files; it's set as an argument so it can be customized at build time.
explanations.17: This pulls the Composer image as a separate stage called 'composer_base' — we'll copy the composer executable from it later, rather than installing Composer ourselves.
explanations.19: This starts the actual application image based on PHP 8.2 with FPM (FastCGI Process Manager), which is used for running PHP in web servers.
explanations.21: Once we're in the main image, we need to redeclare the TIMEZONE argument because arguments don't carry over between FROM statements — each stage starts fresh.
explanations.22: This converts the TIMEZONE argument into an environment variable so the running container will use that timezone.
explanations.27: The 'set -e -x' makes the script exit on any error and print each command before running it, which helps with debugging if something fails.
explanations.28: This checks if the PHPCSFIXER_INSTALL variable equals 'true' — if so, the code inside the 'if' block runs; otherwise it's skipped.
explanations.29: The printf command outputs a colored message to the console during the build to let you know what's happening.
explanations.30: This downloads the PHP-CS-Fixer tool directly from GitHub and saves it to /usr/local/bin so it's available system-wide.
explanations.31: The chmod +x makes the downloaded file executable so you can run it as a command.
explanations.37: Similar to the php-cs-fixer block above, this conditionally installs PHPCBF (a code formatting tool) if the flag is set to true.
explanations.46: We redeclare COMPOSER_HOME here because we need to reference it in the next line, and variables from earlier ARG statements aren't automatically available after a RUN command.
explanations.47: This exports COMPOSER_HOME as an environment variable so Composer knows where to store its cache when the container runs.
explanations.50: This creates the directory structure that Composer needs to cache downloaded packages and version control information.
explanations.52: chmod -R 777 makes the Composer cache directory readable and writable by anyone, so the non-root user we create later can access it.
explanations.54: This copies the 'composer' executable from the composer_base image we pulled earlier into our main image, saving space and build time.
explanations.60: This creates a new non-root Linux user account so the application doesn't run as root (a security best practice); the user is added to 'www-data' and 'root' groups.
explanations.67: The '--no-install-recommends' flag tells apt to skip optional packages, keeping the image smaller by only installing what's strictly needed.
explanations.68: This uses a Docker PHP helper script to compile and install the 'zip' PHP extension, which allows PHP code to handle compressed files.
explanations.69: After installing the extension, we delete temporary PHP source files that were used for compilation but aren't needed in the final image.
explanations.71: This cleans up package manager cache and temporary files to reduce the final image size.
